topic: Myth: Once You're Approved, the Terms Can't Change
objective: Correct a common misconception: 'Once You're Approved, the Terms Can't Change'.

slides.headline: Myth: Approved Terms Can’t Change
slides.subheadline: Read the final offer, conditional approval isn't always final.
slides.visual_concept: Premium editorial photograph: a business owner carefully reading a final loan agreement before signing
slides.image_prompt: Photographic background image only, no text, no logos, no numbers, no UI overlays. a business owner carefully reading a final loan agreement before signing Editorial commercial photography style, shallow depth of field, warm confident mood, colour graded toward deep navy and muted gold tones. No visible cash, coins, calculators, or piggy banks. No readable text or screens with legible content. Square or portrait framing, subject positioned in the lower two-thirds of frame.

slides.headline: What does it mean?
slides.body: Initial or conditional approval can sometimes differ from final terms once full verification is complete, which is why reading the final offer document carefully, and asking about any changes, matters before signing.
slides.visual_concept: Clean off-white panel, one understated gold line icon.

Background only: warm off-white (#F7F5F0) field, generous negative space, one thin gold line icon positioned in the lower third, no text, no photography, no currency symbols.

slides.headline: What's actually true
bullet_points: Conditional approval can differ from final terms
Full verification can affect the final offer
Reading the final document carefully matters
Asking about changes upfront avoids surprises
slides.visual_concept: Matching thin gold line icons on navy, arranged in a simple vertical list.
slides.image_prompt: Create exactly one Instagram carousel slide. The entire canvas is one slide. slides.headline: Worth knowing
bullet_points: Compare the final offer against what was initially discussed
Ask specifically if anything has changed and why
Independent advice is available before signing
A transparent lender explains any changes clearly

slides.headline: Always review the final offer, not just the initial approval.
slides.body: Understanding what can and can't change protects you before you sign.

caption:
It's a reasonable assumption, but not always accurate, initial or conditional approval can be revised once full verification is complete, which is exactly why reading the final offer carefully, rather than assuming it matches the first conversation, is worth the extra few minutes.
